title: A UserRepository with domain errors, transactions and keyset paging
problem: Implement UserRepository in user_repo.py: the one place that writes SQL for the users table. Its methods return User dataclass objects (or None), turn database errors into UsernameTaken and UserNotFound, commit each write as one transaction, and page through users with keyset pagination.
requirements: Edit only user_repo.py; keep the class, method signatures, User, UsernameTaken and UserNotFound
Every value goes through a placeholder
get and by_username return a User or None
add strips the username, rejects a blank one with ValueError, raises UsernameTaken (chained with `from` to the IntegrityError) for a duplicate, commits, and returns the new User
rename strips, rejects blank with ValueError, raises UserNotFound for an unknown id and UsernameTaken for a name in use, commits on success, changes nothing on failure, and returns the updated User
page(after, limit) returns up to limit users ordered by username with username > after (all from the start when after is None); limit outside 1..100 raises ValueError
No write leaves a transaction open, whether it succeeds or fails
contract: UserRepository(conn); add(username: str, now: str) -> User; get(user_id: int) -> User | None; by_username(username: str) -> User | None; rename(user_id: int, new_username: str) -> User; page(after: str | None = None, limit: int = 20) -> list[User]
expectedBehavior: repo.add('  fay ', NOW) returns User(6, 'fay', NOW) and another connection sees it; repo.add('ana', NOW) raises UsernameTaken; repo.page(limit=2) then repo.page(after='ben', limit=2) returns ana, ben, then chen, dara
edgeCases: Unknown id or username: None from the getters
A username with surrounding spaces is stored stripped; a blank one is rejected before any SQL
Duplicate username on add and on rename
Renaming a user id that doesn't exist
Paging past the last user returns []
hints: Conceptual: each public method is a small contract: validate what needs no database, run the SQL in one transaction, translate the few database errors callers care about, and return domain objects. Write one method at a time and run its tests.

Specific: wrap each write in `with self._conn:` and catch sqlite3.IntegrityError outside that block; err.sqlite_errorname == 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE' tells a duplicate from other constraint failures; re-raise as UsernameTaken(...) from err. rename knows the id was unknown when the UPDATE's rowcount is 0; raising inside the with block rolls back. Keyset paging is WHERE username > ? ORDER BY username LIMIT ?.

Implementation: add: name = username.strip(); if not name: raise ValueError; try: with self._conn: cur = self._conn.execute(INSERT ..., (name, now)) except sqlite3.IntegrityError as err: raise UsernameTaken(name) from err; return User(cur.lastrowid, name, now). page with after=None can use WHERE ? IS NULL OR username > ? and pass after twice, or build two fixed SQL strings.
evaluation: No sqlite3 exception or tuple escapes the repository for the cases in the contract
Exactly one transaction per write method; validation happens before it
Errors are chained (raise ... from err) so the original cause stays visible in tracebacks
